title: Batch and streaming: what changes when the data does not wait

videos.script: Saturday, half past ten. The shop in Recife sells its last copy of a book everybody wants. {{shop}} At eleven, a customer orders that book online, for collection in Recife. The website says it is in stock. It is not. {{website}} Nobody finds out until two in the morning, when the nightly job reads the day's sales. The job is not broken. It answers what sold yesterday, and it answers it well. {{night}} The question that went unanswered was a different one. What is happening now? {{now}} This course is about the programs that answer that question. They read each sale the moment it happens, and they never finish. {{stream}} That changes four things. There is no total any more. Time means two things. A crash is a decision. And the program has to be watched, day and night. {{four}} In this lesson you build the machine every other lesson runs on. A virtual machine, a Kafka cluster, and a till that rings up sales. Then you watch the first sales arrive. {{lab}}
